text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says Arab parties have to consult to support Palestinians; stresses Jordan's ties with the Gulf states have been restored to their pre-Gulf crisis levels and coordination with Egypt is at its peak.
- Nine centrist parties expected to announce their merger on Monday in the newly formed National Constitutional Party.
- Japan is considering providing Jordan with around $40 million in aid for human resources development programmes.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says Jordan is ready to provide Qatar with its needs of skilled manpower; senior Qatar officials say they want to expand cooperation with the kingdom.
- Interior minister says the opposition's demand to bring international observers to monitor the November elections is rejected and shameful.
- Jordan's Islamist Action Front (IAF) renews its cooperation pact with the Iraqi Baath party two years after it was signed.
- Foreign Minister Tarawneh says Jordan still awaiting an official request from the United States to shelter Hamas political leader Abu Marzook who is expected to arrive in Amman soon.

- Aqaba Region Authority begins infrastructure work on the Ras-Yemenia area on the southern coast of Aqaba city; signs a 3.7 million dinar ($5.2 million) contract with the Bardeeni company to undertake the project.
- Interior minister says will not allow any infringement on public land by people building homes illegally.
- Trade and Supply Minister Hani Mulqi says after end of U.S. visit that American investors are convinced of the viability of Aqaba as a regional entrepot.
- Jordan, Israel to inaugurate Baqoura peace park on Tuesday.
- King's nephew Prince Ghazi engaged to Omani
